newsitem.title: USA: Dole says Clinton cannot be trusted in debate.
newsitem.headline: Dole says Clinton cannot be trusted in debate.

text.p: With the campaign's first presidential debate only days away, Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole told Americans on Tuesday not to believe what President Bill Clinton will say.

Speaking in a gymnasium packed with supporters at Lakeland Community College in this suburb of Cleveland, Dole portrayed himself as a man whose word is his bond while he painted the president as a man who has left a string of broken campaign promises behind him.

"When you are listening to the debates, ask yourself this question: 'Would you buy a used campaign promise from this man?," Dole asked a cheering crowd in his first campaign appearance since visiting a Miami delicatessen last Saturday.

Since last Thursday Dole has been obsessed with preparations for Sunday's 90-minute encounter with Clinton in Hartford, Conn. He spent four days at his Florida apartment preparing and planned to do the same this week.
He mocked Clinton's failure to deliver a middle class tax cut as he promised in the 1992 campaign and asked, "Have any of you seen this cut?"
As shouts of no echoed across the hall, Dole said, "Bill Clinton makes promises that are liberal and makes promises that are conservative. But the only prosmises he keeps are his liberal promises."

He then offered a consumer guide to the debate. "Buyer beware, what you see is not what you get. The real cost is way over list price. High maintenance costs will shoot up unexpectedly. The politician veers uncontrollably to the left except in the face of oncoming elections when he rolls to the right."
Dole added, "And that's why on Nov. 5 the American people are going to demand a factory recall of Bill Clinton and his liberal policies."
Before the speech Dole visited a local family, Don and Jean DiSantis, for coffee in their backyard.
He told them his 15 percent tax cut plan would give them more money and as he left reporters asked him what could be accomplished by the Israeli-Palestinian summit.
"I'm not certain. Look at the pattern of this administration -- photo op foreign policy."
He said that what should happen would be the end of violence and added, "We'll see what happens."
